title: WCLI-98 follow-up: the refused-header detail is dropped by reporting.ts and profiles.ts, and no test drives it to stderr
description: From the Opus review of ward-cli#215 at a513c52 (finding 5). reporting.ts:85-87 and :249-252 and profiles.ts:210-214 catch the profile refusal and drop the refusedHeader detail, so the name is not printed on those paths. Both fail safe and leak nothing. Suggestion: a runWard test drives a refused name to stderr and asserts the canonical suffix there. Not built in ward-cli#215.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Each path that catches a profile refusal either carries the canonical refusedHeader detail or is shown to need none
A runWard test drives a refused header name to stderr and asserts the canonical suffix and that no declared byte is printed

implementationNotes: Built on feat/wcli-116-refused-header-detail-cli as test/refused-header-cli.test.ts, no source change. Finding: the paths that print an error (profile approve, run) already carry the canonical suffix; the paths that catch the refusal (profiles.ts:210-214 for profile list and check; reporting.ts:85-87 and :249-252 for status and doctor) report an enumerated state ("declaration": "invalid", reasons ["declaration"], binding unknown, state_malformed) with no free-text field, so there is no place for a name and none is added. 15 runWard cases: approve and run print "(refused header: <canonical>)" and never the declared spelling or any value; list, check, status and doctor print their state and neither the declared name, the canonical name, nor a value; an unlisted header is never printed on any path. Mutation controls: dropping the suffix and echoing the declared name each reddened exactly the 6 approve and run cases. No reporting-path mutation was run, since those paths have no detail channel to mutate. Whether status and doctor should name the header is a design question, not decided here. Acceptance criteria left unchecked pending review.

Round 1 review (Opus, ward-cli#218 at ba0cf6a) REQUEST_CHANGES, fixed in the next commit. All four catch sites are now covered: (a) profiles.ts:210-214 (profile list, check) and (b) reporting.ts:249-252 (status, doctor) report enumerated states; (c) profiles.ts stillApproved (manifest rewritten to a refused name while the approval prompt is open) is refused with a fixed message, no approval stored, no name printed; (d) reporting.ts stale-approval report emits a constant "cannot be read" sentence, no name printed. None carries a detail channel and none needs one. Test changes: the stored credential and the header value are sentinels asserted absent from stdout and stderr in every case (the secret-header case also carries the value on an ordinary header); a positive control drives run and profile list on the same damaged vault and asserts the vault_state_malformed suffix names X-Forwarded-Host; reporting cases also run in text mode; the unlisted-header test now needs a per-command marker; a refused run persists nothing (empty audit history). Mutation controls: replacing the load-path rethrow with a plain malformed() reddened exactly the two positive-control tests (status and doctor stay green, as designed); echoing the header value into the detail reddened the 4 ordinary-header approve/run cases and the 2 load positive controls. Line citation drift (reporting.ts:85-87) noted: that range is the wardCode helper.

Header-auth mutation, prediction recorded before the run: echoing the whole declaration (which carries the value sentinel on an ordinary header) at the secret-header refusal site, with the constructor filter removed, turns exactly 2 cases red, "profile approve" and "run" for "the secret header's name", and the assertion that fires is the value-sentinel absence check in printedOf. profile list and check swallow the refusal and print only a state, and no stored-snapshot case uses auth.name, so those stay green. Result: exactly those 2 cases went red, and both failed on "Expected to not contain: value-sentinel-9c1e" with the declaration visible in the printed message. The header-auth value assertion therefore bites. The mutation was restored (git checkout src).

Round 2 review (Opus, ward-cli#218 at 4e89070) REQUEST_CHANGES, fix round. N1: the vault stores the credential base64-encoded and only run.ts decodes it after approval, so the SECRET check looked for a form no refusal path produces; the test now also measures Buffer.from(SECRET).toString("base64") absent. Prediction recorded before the run: a mutation echoing the stored secrets array at the vault-state.ts re-raise (constructor filter removed) turns exactly 2 cases red, the damaged-vault run and profile list suffix cases, failing on the base64 sentinel and not on the header value, because only the secrets array is echoed. Result: exactly those 2 went red, both on "Expected to not contain: c3ludGhldGljLXNlY3JldC1zZW50aW5lbC0zZDdi" (the base64 sentinel). Earlier value-echo mutation re-run to say which assertion fired: the 4 ordinary-header approve/run cases and the 2 damaged-vault cases failed on "Expected to not contain: value-sentinel-9c1e" (the value check in printedOf); the audit-empty case failed on the missing canonical suffix because the detail was the value. N2: the stale-approval case asserts "declaration of this profile cannot be read". N3: the prompt-rewrite case asserts code profile_changed. N4: the audit-empty case now approves a valid profile first so the run would reach admission, with a positive control that an admitted run writes audit events in this harness; approvals()===0 asserted in the six approve/run refusal cases. Remainder: the text-mode cases have exact positive markers (invalid declaration; the declaration is not one Ward can use; binding: unknown; schema fail state_malformed). N5 and the status absence in the unlisted-header test left as is. Fix diff base: 4e89070f0.

Correction to the earlier round-2 note ("Round 2 review (Opus, ward-cli#218 at 4e89070) REQUEST_CHANGES, fix round"), item N4: its claim that the audit-empty case approves a valid profile "so the run would reach admission" is wrong. With the refusal removed, run stops at profile_approval_stale (run.ts:161-162), before writeAudit (run.ts:399), so the empty-history assertion cannot be the first thing to fail; the case's teeth are the refusal suffix assertion. The earlier note is left as written and corrected here, per the opum-doc ruling under DEC-172 (4ab) (opum-ai/opum-doc#1528, a note on ODOC-552). The test comment is struck to match, and the printedOf comment no longer claims every case goes through it (the positive-control count cases do not). No assertion or code changed. Reviewer fix (a) (the empty-audit assertion firing first, and the control read through printedOf) is a follow-up task, not a gate on ward-cli#218.

Design decision cited in place of the earlier "design question, not decided here" wording (that note is left as written): DEC-250, ruled A by opum-doc (opum-ai/opum-doc#1527, a note on ODOC-552): the reporting commands (status, doctor, profile list, check) keep a refused header enumerated with no name; the canonical name stays on the commands that fail with an error (approve, run, and run / profile list on a damaged vault). No ADR is required. Landed as squash 7095663e2a5c56c6f1a713587275eec8ff5ede9d (ward-cli#218). Reviews: round 1 REQUEST_CHANGES at ba0cf6a; round 2 REQUEST_CHANGES at 4e89070 with AC0 and AC1 MET; one confirmatory review at d4df418 with every round-2 finding fixed except one minor item, resolved by the opum-doc ruling under DEC-172 (4ab) (opum-ai/opum-doc#1528, ODOC-552): comment-only fix at 17d5305, the empty-audit assertion follow-up filed as WCLI-118 and not a gate.
finalSummary: Adds test/refused-header-cli.test.ts, 25 runWard cases through the real store, keychain provider and normalizer, landed as squash 7095663e2a5c56c6f1a713587275eec8ff5ede9d (ward-cli#218). No source change. Approve and run print the canonical "(refused header: <name>)" suffix and never the declared spelling, a header value or the stored credential (plain and base64 forms); run and profile list on a damaged vault print the vault_state_malformed suffix. All four catch sites (profiles.ts list/check, reporting.ts status/doctor, profiles.ts stillApproved, the stale-approval report) report an enumerated state or fixed sentence with no name, which DEC-250 (opum-doc#1527) rules is the intended design. Evidence for AC0: round 2 Opus review MET, the confirmatory review at d4df418, and the DEC-172 (4ab) ruling (opum-doc#1528); for AC1: the suffix, no-declared-byte, no-value and no-secret assertions, with mutation controls whose red sets were predicted in advance and recorded on this task. CI green at 17d5305, bun run check 1077 pass. Follow-up: WCLI-118 (the empty-audit assertion cannot fire first; control not through printedOf), normal priority, not started.
